When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. Under time pressure the instruction was to submit in less than 10 seconds and “Be quick!” Under time delay it was to think for more than 20 seconds before submitting and “Carefully consider your decision.” Noncompliance was said to make the decision very likely invalid, in which case neither person would be paid the money allocated. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is the person’s Part A giving decision. Output only the actual amount given as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

Every cent given is doubled for the recipient. If you give x and the other gives y, potential Part A earnings in cents are 50−x+2y for you and 50−y+2x for the other. Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. Decisions are simultaneous and one shot: the other person’s choice is not known while deciding, and there is no repeated interaction. No feedback about the other’s choice or actual earnings is supplied before the current response. Participants practised a whole-number slider before the study; moving it sets a value, and clicking Continue submits the response. They were told there are three study parts, one randomly chosen afterward to determine additional earnings; earnings for that selected part do not depend on decisions in the other parts. Contents of upcoming parts were not announced before Part A. Completing the study pays a fixed US$0.25 in addition to the chosen part’s applicable earnings; payments in pounds use the announced rate US$1.00=£0.80. Before Part A, instructions could be read at the person’s own pace. A transition screen explained the time condition for at most 30 seconds, with earlier continuation allowed. When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. Under time pressure the instruction was to submit in less than 10 seconds and “Be quick!” Under time delay it was to think for more than 20 seconds before submitting and “Carefully consider your decision.” Noncompliance was said to make the decision very likely invalid, in which case neither person would be paid the money allocated. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is the person’s Part A giving decision. Output only the actual amount given as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

In Part A, two real participants each receive 50 US cents, separately decide how much to give to the other, and keep the remainder. The whole-cent giving amount can be any integer from 0 through 50. Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. Decisions are simultaneous and one shot: the other person’s choice is not known while deciding, and there is no repeated interaction. No feedback about the other’s choice or actual earnings is supplied before the current response. Participants practised a whole-number slider before the study; moving it sets a value, and clicking Continue submits the response. Contents of upcoming parts were not announced before Part A. Completing the study pays a fixed US$0.25 in addition to the chosen part’s applicable earnings; payments in pounds use the announced rate US$1.00=£0.80. Before Part A, instructions could be read at the person’s own pace. A transition screen explained the time condition for at most 30 seconds, with earlier continuation allowed. When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. Under time pressure the instruction was to submit in less than 10 seconds and “Be quick!” Under time delay it was to think for more than 20 seconds before submitting and “Carefully consider your decision.” Noncompliance was said to make the decision very likely invalid, in which case neither person would be paid the money allocated. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is Part B, a separate incentivized belief report after the person’s Part A choice and two manipulation-check screens. The time restriction has been lifted: the rest is completed at the person’s own pace. Report how many of the other person’s original 50 cents they think that person shared with them. If Part B is selected for payment, an estimate within 5 cents of the other’s actual giving earns US$0.50; an error greater than 5 cents earns zero for this question. Predict the person’s stated estimate, not the unknown actual partner transfer. Earlier own choices and already-given check answers are history, not baseline personality traits. The other’s actual transfer and resulting payoffs remain unknown. Output only the actual estimated amount as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

Every cent given is doubled for the recipient. If you give x and the other gives y, potential Part A earnings in cents are 50−x+2y for you and 50−y+2x for the other. Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. Decisions are simultaneous and one shot: the other person’s choice is not known while deciding, and there is no repeated interaction. No feedback about the other’s choice or actual earnings is supplied before the current response. Participants practised a whole-number slider before the study; moving it sets a value, and clicking Continue submits the response. They were told there are three study parts, one randomly chosen afterward to determine additional earnings; earnings for that selected part do not depend on decisions in the other parts. Contents of upcoming parts were not announced before Part A. Completing the study pays a fixed US$0.25 in addition to the chosen part’s applicable earnings; payments in pounds use the announced rate US$1.00=£0.80. Before Part A, instructions could be read at the person’s own pace. A transition screen explained the time condition for at most 30 seconds, with earlier continuation allowed. When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. Under time pressure the instruction was to submit in less than 10 seconds and “Be quick!” Under time delay it was to think for more than 20 seconds before submitting and “Carefully consider your decision.” Noncompliance was said to make the decision very likely invalid, in which case neither person would be paid the money allocated. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is Part B, a separate incentivized belief report after the person’s Part A choice and two manipulation-check screens. The time restriction has been lifted: the rest is completed at the person’s own pace. Report how many of the other person’s original 50 cents they think that person shared with them. If Part B is selected for payment, an estimate within 5 cents of the other’s actual giving earns US$0.50; an error greater than 5 cents earns zero for this question. Predict the person’s stated estimate, not the unknown actual partner transfer. Earlier own choices and already-given check answers are history, not baseline personality traits. The other’s actual transfer and resulting payoffs remain unknown. Output only the actual estimated amount as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

Predict one person’s actual response in the indicated part of an anonymous online study. When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. Under time pressure the instruction was to submit in less than 10 seconds and “Be quick!” Under time delay it was to think for more than 20 seconds before submitting and “Carefully consider your decision.” Noncompliance was said to make the decision very likely invalid, in which case neither person would be paid the money allocated. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is the person’s Part A giving decision. Output only the actual amount given as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. Decisions are simultaneous and one shot: the other person’s choice is not known while deciding, and there is no repeated interaction. No feedback about the other’s choice or actual earnings is supplied before the current response. If Part B is selected for payment, an estimate within 5 cents of the other’s actual giving earns US$0.50; an error greater than 5 cents earns zero for this question. Predict the person’s stated estimate, not the unknown actual partner transfer. Earlier own choices and already-given check answers are history, not baseline personality traits. Every cent given is doubled for the recipient. If you give x and the other gives y, potential Part A earnings in cents are 50−x+2y for you and 50−y+2x for the other. Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. Decisions are simultaneous and one shot: the other person’s choice is not known while deciding, and there is no repeated interaction. No feedback about the other’s choice or actual earnings is supplied before the current response. Participants practised a whole-number slider before the study; moving it sets a value, and clicking Continue submits the response. They were told there are three study parts, one randomly chosen afterward to determine additional earnings; earnings for that selected part do not depend on decisions in the other parts. Contents of upcoming parts were not announced before Part A. Completing the study pays a fixed US$0.25 in addition to the chosen part’s applicable earnings; payments in pounds use the announced rate US$1.00=£0.80. Before Part A, instructions could be read at the person’s own pace. A transition screen explained the time condition for at most 30 seconds, with earlier continuation allowed. When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. Under time pressure the instruction was to submit in less than 10 seconds and “Be quick!” Under time delay it was to think for more than 20 seconds before submitting and “Carefully consider your decision.” Noncompliance was said to make the decision very likely invalid, in which case neither person would be paid the money allocated. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is Part B, a separate incentivized belief report after the person’s Part A choice and two manipulation-check screens. The time restriction has been lifted: the rest is completed at the person’s own pace. Report how many of the other person’s original 50 cents they think that person shared with them. If Part B is selected for payment, an estimate within 5 cents of the other’s actual giving earns US$0.50; an error greater than 5 cents earns zero for this question. Predict the person’s stated estimate, not the unknown actual partner transfer. Earlier own choices and already-given check answers are history, not baseline personality traits. The other’s actual transfer and resulting payoffs remain unknown. Output only the actual estimated amount as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

Predict one person’s actual response in the indicated part of an anonymous online study. In Part A, two real participants each receive 50 US cents, separately decide how much to give to the other, and keep the remainder. The whole-cent giving amount can be any integer from 0 through 50. Every cent given is doubled for the recipient. If you give x and the other gives y, potential Part A earnings in cents are 50−x+2y for you and 50−y+2x for the other. Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. Decisions are simultaneous and one shot: the other person’s choice is not known while deciding, and there is no repeated interaction. No feedback about the other’s choice or actual earnings is supplied before the current response. Participants practised a whole-number slider before the study; moving it sets a value, and clicking Continue submits the response. They were told there are three study parts, one randomly chosen afterward to determine additional earnings; earnings for that selected part do not depend on decisions in the other parts. Contents of upcoming parts were not announced before Part A. Completing the study pays a fixed US$0.25 in addition to the chosen part’s applicable earnings; payments in pounds use the announced rate US$1.00=£0.80. Before Part A, instructions could be read at the person’s own pace. A transition screen explained the time condition for at most 30 seconds, with earlier continuation allowed. When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. Under time pressure the instruction was to submit in less than 10 seconds and “Be quick!” Under time delay it was to think for more than 20 seconds before submitting and “Carefully consider your decision.” Noncompliance was said to make the decision very likely invalid, in which case neither person would be paid the money allocated. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is the person’s Part A giving decision. Output only the actual amount given as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

Predict one person’s actual response in the indicated part of an anonymous online study. In Part A, two real participants each receive 50 US cents, separately decide how much to give to the other, and keep the remainder. The whole-cent giving amount can be any integer from 0 through 50. Every cent given is doubled for the recipient. If you give x and the other gives y, potential Part A earnings in cents are 50−x+2y for you and 50−y+2x for the other. Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. Decisions are simultaneous and one shot: the other person’s choice is not known while deciding, and there is no repeated interaction. No feedback about the other’s choice or actual earnings is supplied before the current response. Participants practised a whole-number slider before the study; moving it sets a value, and clicking Continue submits the response. They were told there are three study parts, one randomly chosen afterward to determine additional earnings; earnings for that selected part do not depend on decisions in the other parts. Contents of upcoming parts were not announced before Part A. Completing the study pays a fixed US$0.25 in addition to the chosen part’s applicable earnings; payments in pounds use the announced rate US$1.00=£0.80. Before Part A, instructions could be read at the person’s own pace. A transition screen explained the time condition for at most 30 seconds, with earlier continuation allowed. When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. Under time pressure the instruction was to submit in less than 10 seconds and “Be quick!” Under time delay it was to think for more than 20 seconds before submitting and “Carefully consider your decision.” Noncompliance was said to make the decision very likely invalid, in which case neither person would be paid the money allocated. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is Part B, a separate incentivized belief report after the person’s Part A choice and two manipulation-check screens. The time restriction has been lifted: the rest is completed at the person’s own pace. Report how many of the other person’s original 50 cents they think that person shared with them. If Part B is selected for payment, an estimate within 5 cents of the other’s actual giving earns US$0.50; an error greater than 5 cents earns zero for this question. Predict the person’s stated estimate, not the unknown actual partner transfer. Earlier own choices and already-given check answers are history, not baseline personality traits. The other’s actual transfer and resulting payoffs remain unknown. Output only the actual estimated amount as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

Predict one person’s actual response in the indicated part of an anonymous online study. In Part A, two real participants each receive 50 US cents, separately decide how much to give to the other, and keep the remainder. The whole-cent giving amount can be any integer from 0 through 50. Every cent given is doubled for the recipient. If you give x and the other gives y, potential Part A earnings in cents are 50−x+2y for you and 50−y+2x for the other. Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. Decisions are simultaneous and one shot: the other person’s choice is not known while deciding, and there is no repeated interaction. No feedback about the other’s choice or actual earnings is supplied before the current response. Participants practised a whole-number slider before the study; moving it sets a value, and clicking Continue submits the response. They were told there are three study parts, one randomly chosen afterward to determine additional earnings; earnings for that selected part do not depend on decisions in the other parts. Contents of upcoming parts were not announced before Part A. Completing the study pays a fixed US$0.25 in addition to the chosen part’s applicable earnings; payments in pounds use the announced rate US$1.00=£0.80. Before Part A, instructions could be read at the person’s own pace. A transition screen explained the time condition for at most 30 seconds, with earlier continuation allowed. When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. Under time pressure the instruction was to submit in less than 10 seconds and “Be quick!” Under time delay it was to think for more than 20 seconds before submitting and “Carefully consider your decision.” Noncompliance was said to make the decision very likely invalid, in which case neither person would be paid the money allocated. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is Part B, a separate incentivized belief report after the person’s Part A choice and two manipulation-check screens. The time restriction has been lifted: the rest is completed at the person’s own pace. Report how many of the other person’s original 50 cents they think that person shared with them. If Part B is selected for payment, an estimate within 5 cents of the other’s actual giving earns US$0.50; an error greater than 5 cents earns zero for this question. Predict the person’s stated estimate, not the unknown actual partner transfer. Earlier own choices and already-given check answers are history, not baseline personality traits. The other’s actual transfer and resulting payoffs remain unknown. Output only the actual estimated amount as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. Decisions are simultaneous and one shot: the other person’s choice is not known while deciding, and there is no repeated interaction. No feedback about the other’s choice or actual earnings is supplied before the current response. Participants practised a whole-number slider before the study; moving it sets a value, and clicking Continue submits the response. They were told there are three study parts, one randomly chosen afterward to determine additional earnings; earnings for that selected part do not depend on decisions in the other parts. Contents of upcoming parts were not announced before Part A. Completing the study pays a fixed US$0.25 in addition to the chosen part’s applicable earnings; payments in pounds use the announced rate US$1.00=£0.80. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is Part B, a separate incentivized belief report after the person’s Part A choice and two manipulation-check screens. The time restriction has been lifted: the rest is completed at the person’s own pace. Report how many of the other person’s original 50 cents they think that person shared with them. If Part B is selected for payment, an estimate within 5 cents of the other’s actual giving earns US$0.50; an error greater than 5 cents earns zero for this question. Predict the person’s stated estimate, not the unknown actual partner transfer. Earlier own choices and already-given check answers are history, not baseline personality traits. The other’s actual transfer and resulting payoffs remain unknown. Output only the actual estimated amount as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

Every cent given is doubled for the recipient. If you give x and the other gives y, potential Part A earnings in cents are 50−x+2y for you and 50−y+2x for the other. Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. Decisions are simultaneous and one shot: the other person’s choice is not known while deciding, and there is no repeated interaction. No feedback about the other’s choice or actual earnings is supplied before the current response. Participants practised a whole-number slider before the study; moving it sets a value, and clicking Continue submits the response. They were told there are three study parts, one randomly chosen afterward to determine additional earnings; earnings for that selected part do not depend on decisions in the other parts. Contents of upcoming parts were not announced before Part A. Completing the study pays a fixed US$0.25 in addition to the chosen part’s applicable earnings; payments in pounds use the announced rate US$1.00=£0.80. Before Part A, instructions could be read at the person’s own pace. A transition screen explained the time condition for at most 30 seconds, with earlier continuation allowed. When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. Under time pressure the instruction was to submit in less than 10 seconds and “Be quick!” Under time delay it was to think for more than 20 seconds before submitting and “Carefully consider your decision.” Noncompliance was said to make the decision very likely invalid, in which case neither person would be paid the money allocated. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is the person’s Part A giving decision. Output only the actual amount given as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

Predict one person’s actual response in the indicated part of an anonymous online study. In Part A, two real participants each receive 50 US cents, separately decide how much to give to the other, and keep the remainder. The whole-cent giving amount can be any integer from 0 through 50. Every cent given is doubled for the recipient. If you give x and the other gives y, potential Part A earnings in cents are 50−x+2y for you and 50−y+2x for the other. Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. Decisions are simultaneous and one shot: the other person’s choice is not known while deciding, and there is no repeated interaction. No feedback about the other’s choice or actual earnings is supplied before the current response. Participants practised a whole-number slider before the study; moving it sets a value, and clicking Continue submits the response. They were told there are three study parts, one randomly chosen afterward to determine additional earnings; earnings for that selected part do not depend on decisions in the other parts. Contents of upcoming parts were not announced before Part A. Completing the study pays a fixed US$0.25 in addition to the chosen part’s applicable earnings; payments in pounds use the announced rate US$1.00=£0.80. Before Part A, instructions could be read at the person’s own pace. A transition screen explained the time condition for at most 30 seconds, with earlier continuation allowed. When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. Under time pressure the instruction was to submit in less than 10 seconds and “Be quick!” Under time delay it was to think for more than 20 seconds before submitting and “Carefully consider your decision.” Noncompliance was said to make the decision very likely invalid, in which case neither person would be paid the money allocated. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is Part B, a separate incentivized belief report after the person’s Part A choice and two manipulation-check screens. The time restriction has been lifted: the rest is completed at the person’s own pace. Report how many of the other person’s original 50 cents they think that person shared with them. If Part B is selected for payment, an estimate within 5 cents of the other’s actual giving earns US$0.50; an error greater than 5 cents earns zero for this question. Predict the person’s stated estimate, not the unknown actual partner transfer. Earlier own choices and already-given check answers are history, not baseline personality traits. The other’s actual transfer and resulting payoffs remain unknown. Output only the actual estimated amount as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

Every cent given is doubled for the recipient. If you give x and the other gives y, potential Part A earnings in cents are 50−x+2y for you and 50−y+2x for the other. Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. Decisions are simultaneous and one shot: the other person’s choice is not known while deciding, and there is no repeated interaction. No feedback about the other’s choice or actual earnings is supplied before the current response. Participants practised a whole-number slider before the study; moving it sets a value, and clicking Continue submits the response. They were told there are three study parts, one randomly chosen afterward to determine additional earnings; earnings for that selected part do not depend on decisions in the other parts. Contents of upcoming parts were not announced before Part A. Completing the study pays a fixed US$0.25 in addition to the chosen part’s applicable earnings; payments in pounds use the announced rate US$1.00=£0.80. Before Part A, instructions could be read at the person’s own pace. A transition screen explained the time condition for at most 30 seconds, with earlier continuation allowed. When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. Under time pressure the instruction was to submit in less than 10 seconds and “Be quick!” Under time delay it was to think for more than 20 seconds before submitting and “Carefully consider your decision.” Noncompliance was said to make the decision very likely invalid, in which case neither person would be paid the money allocated. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is Part B, a separate incentivized belief report after the person’s Part A choice and two manipulation-check screens. The time restriction has been lifted: the rest is completed at the person’s own pace. Report how many of the other person’s original 50 cents they think that person shared with them. If Part B is selected for payment, an estimate within 5 cents of the other’s actual giving earns US$0.50; an error greater than 5 cents earns zero for this question. Predict the person’s stated estimate, not the unknown actual partner transfer. Earlier own choices and already-given check answers are history, not baseline personality traits. The other’s actual transfer and resulting payoffs remain unknown. Output only the actual estimated amount as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

Predict one person’s actual response in the indicated part of an anonymous online study. In Part A, two real participants each receive 50 US cents, separately decide how much to give to the other, and keep the remainder. The whole-cent giving amount can be any integer from 0 through 50. Every cent given is doubled for the recipient. If you give x and the other gives y, potential Part A earnings in cents are 50−x+2y for you and 50−y+2x for the other. Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. Decisions are simultaneous and one shot: the other person’s choice is not known while deciding, and there is no repeated interaction. No feedback about the other’s choice or actual earnings is supplied before the current response. Participants practised a whole-number slider before the study; moving it sets a value, and clicking Continue submits the response. They were told there are three study parts, one randomly chosen afterward to determine additional earnings; earnings for that selected part do not depend on decisions in the other parts. Contents of upcoming parts were not announced before Part A. Completing the study pays a fixed US$0.25 in addition to the chosen part’s applicable earnings; payments in pounds use the announced rate US$1.00=£0.80. Before Part A, instructions could be read at the person’s own pace. A transition screen explained the time condition for at most 30 seconds, with earlier continuation allowed. When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. Under time pressure the instruction was to submit in less than 10 seconds and “Be quick!” Under time delay it was to think for more than 20 seconds before submitting and “Carefully consider your decision.” Noncompliance was said to make the decision very likely invalid, in which case neither person would be paid the money allocated. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is Part B, a separate incentivized belief report after the person’s Part A choice and two manipulation-check screens. The time restriction has been lifted: the rest is completed at the person’s own pace. Report how many of the other person’s original 50 cents they think that person shared with them. If Part B is selected for payment, an estimate within 5 cents of the other’s actual giving earns US$0.50; an error greater than 5 cents earns zero for this question. Predict the person’s stated estimate, not the unknown actual partner transfer. Earlier own choices and already-given check answers are history, not baseline personality traits. The other’s actual transfer and resulting payoffs remain unknown. Output only the actual estimated amount as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. Decisions are simultaneous and one shot: the other person’s choice is not known while deciding, and there is no repeated interaction. No feedback about the other’s choice or actual earnings is supplied before the current response. When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. Under time pressure the instruction was to submit in less than 10 seconds and “Be quick!” Under time delay it was to think for more than 20 seconds before submitting and “Carefully consider your decision.” Noncompliance was said to make the decision very likely invalid, in which case neither person would be paid the money allocated. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is Part B, a separate incentivized belief report after the person’s Part A choice and two manipulation-check screens. The time restriction has been lifted: the rest is completed at the person’s own pace. Report how many of the other person’s original 50 cents they think that person shared with them. If Part B is selected for payment, an estimate within 5 cents of the other’s actual giving earns US$0.50; an error greater than 5 cents earns zero for this question. Predict the person’s stated estimate, not the unknown actual partner transfer. Earlier own choices and already-given check answers are history, not baseline personality traits. The other’s actual transfer and resulting payoffs remain unknown. Output only the actual estimated amount as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is the person’s Part A giving decision. Output only the actual amount given as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

Every cent given is doubled for the recipient. If you give x and the other gives y, potential Part A earnings in cents are 50−x+2y for you and 50−y+2x for the other. Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. Decisions are simultaneous and one shot: the other person’s choice is not known while deciding, and there is no repeated interaction. No feedback about the other’s choice or actual earnings is supplied before the current response. Participants practised a whole-number slider before the study; moving it sets a value, and clicking Continue submits the response. They were told there are three study parts, one randomly chosen afterward to determine additional earnings; earnings for that selected part do not depend on decisions in the other parts. Contents of upcoming parts were not announced before Part A. Completing the study pays a fixed US$0.25 in addition to the chosen part’s applicable earnings; payments in pounds use the announced rate US$1.00=£0.80. Before Part A, instructions could be read at the person’s own pace. A transition screen explained the time condition for at most 30 seconds, with earlier continuation allowed. When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. Under time pressure the instruction was to submit in less than 10 seconds and “Be quick!” Under time delay it was to think for more than 20 seconds before submitting and “Carefully consider your decision.” Noncompliance was said to make the decision very likely invalid, in which case neither person would be paid the money allocated. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is the person’s Part A giving decision. Output only the actual amount given as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

Every cent given is doubled for the recipient. If you give x and the other gives y, potential Part A earnings in cents are 50−x+2y for you and 50−y+2x for the other. Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. Decisions are simultaneous and one shot: the other person’s choice is not known while deciding, and there is no repeated interaction. No feedback about the other’s choice or actual earnings is supplied before the current response. Participants practised a whole-number slider before the study; moving it sets a value, and clicking Continue submits the response. They were told there are three study parts, one randomly chosen afterward to determine additional earnings; earnings for that selected part do not depend on decisions in the other parts. Contents of upcoming parts were not announced before Part A. Completing the study pays a fixed US$0.25 in addition to the chosen part’s applicable earnings; payments in pounds use the announced rate US$1.00=£0.80. Before Part A, instructions could be read at the person’s own pace. A transition screen explained the time condition for at most 30 seconds, with earlier continuation allowed. When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. Under time pressure the instruction was to submit in less than 10 seconds and “Be quick!” Under time delay it was to think for more than 20 seconds before submitting and “Carefully consider your decision.” Noncompliance was said to make the decision very likely invalid, in which case neither person would be paid the money allocated. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is Part B, a separate incentivized belief report after the person’s Part A choice and two manipulation-check screens. The time restriction has been lifted: the rest is completed at the person’s own pace. Report how many of the other person’s original 50 cents they think that person shared with them. If Part B is selected for payment, an estimate within 5 cents of the other’s actual giving earns US$0.50; an error greater than 5 cents earns zero for this question. Predict the person’s stated estimate, not the unknown actual partner transfer. Earlier own choices and already-given check answers are history, not baseline personality traits. The other’s actual transfer and resulting payoffs remain unknown. Output only the actual estimated amount as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.

Both giving 0 earns 50 each; both giving 50 earns 100 each; keeping 50 while the other gives 50 earns 150 for you and 0 for them. When a partner profile was supplied, it appeared two seconds before the slider and clock. No exact invalidation probability was announced. Do not assume a recorded choice was invalidated or infer realized earnings. Only the partner information explicitly supplied below was revealed; no identity profile means no inferred partner religion or other profile details. Previous Prolific religious self-description is historical and need not equal current religious identity. Stable self attributes and a report of concrete PD-experiment experience before today are supplied without inventing attitudes or treating later game-understanding tests as prior knowledge. The current task is the person’s Part A giving decision. Output only the actual amount given as an integer from 0 to 50, in US cents, without explanation.
